COMMUNITY & PAYMENTS

In Goma, Life Without Banks Turns to Bitcoin

With local financial institutions shuttered for over a year, Gloire Kambale Wanzavalere’s Bridge Sats runs community transactions on Fedi.

When commercial banks in Goma shut their doors more than twelve months ago, the city’s commerce faced a total institutional freeze. Rather than waiting for traditional financial channels to resume operations, local builders stepped forward with sovereign alternatives.

Gloire Kambale Wanzavalere dropped out of his university law programme six years ago to focus entirely on Bitcoin development. Today, he operates Bridge Sats—an over-the-counter desk and settlement service serving the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The project runs an active federation on the Fedi protocol, where community payments provide an essential lifeline.

In Goma, the banks have been closed for over a year. Gloire Kambale Wanzavalere didn't wait for them to reopen. Fedi highlighted in a builder profile on Thursday, noting that daily transaction settlement remains the primary driver behind local adoption.

Source: Fedi on Jumble

SECURITY AUDIT

Sparrow Wallet Ships Version 2.5.4 Following Major Security Reviews

Craig Raw publishes a hardened release incorporating extensive researcher findings and community contributions.

Desktop Bitcoin wallet Sparrow released version 2.5.4 on Thursday morning, concluding a comprehensive round of security audits across its codebase.

Developer Craig Raw announced the milestone alongside gratitude for the collective auditing effort: Sparrow v2.5.4 has been released, delivering the results of several extensive security reviews. Raw expressed thanks to all contributors and independent researchers who submitted findings.

The release follows a wave of software auditing across the ecosystem, including deterministic firmware verification in Frostsnap 0.4.0 and tenant safety warnings in Flint 1.0.1.

Source: craigraw on Jumble

DEVELOPER TOOLS

Horcrux 1.0.1 and Routstr Updates Expand Tooling

Matt Lorentz polishes cryptographic backups while Routstr rolls out Cashu wallet migration and Pi Agent integration.

Following its initial major milestone, sensitive backup utility Horcrux received an update from creator Matt Lorentz. Just dropped Horcrux 1.0.1 with fixes for a few bugs I found in my final testing before 1.0. Lorentz noted, continuing to gather questions for the documentation FAQ.

Meanwhile, AI inference routing daemon routstrd reached version 0.4.2. Developer routstr announced that This version brings brings more stability to the entire stack. Key enhancements include migration to a Coco-Cashu based wallet to improve mint rate-limit resilience, Tinfoil model caching, Windows OS support, and Pi Agent integration with configurable thinking modes.

Sources: Matt Lorentz on Jumble · routstr on Jumble
